QUOTE_UNVERIFIED cleared for the same reason. 'BRANCH' / icon / 'LEVEL 1' are all visible in my read of the frame. XMLItem.as:130 is verbatim 'this.levelrestriction = xml.minlvl;'. The field census is EXACT and I ran it myself: 'grep -n "itemPanel\." InventoryUI.as' yields only selectItem, selectItemName, selectItemAttribute and chatbutton (plus visible / add-removeEventListener) - there is no level field on the Android item panel. InventoryUI.as:1453-1462 confirms what the panel is actually fed. Correctly scoped: HELD that the label exists and reads 'LEVEL 1' for an unmodified Branch; UNHELD what computes it.

All four cites resolve verbatim: MCSCharacter.as:120, :141-146, :56-62 (PART_l_shoulder = 23 .. PART_r_knee = 26), MCSWolf.as:188 and :197. The type tell it points at is real and checkable - :10 through :52 declare ':int', :54 through :62 declare ':*'. Correct boundary (human 0..22).

Self-contradictory on the boundary index, and the contradiction is inside one sentence. It states 'a 23-deep addChild stack (partListLength 22, loop i <= partListLength)' - which is indices 0..22 - and then assigns 'PART_prop3/l_shoulder/r_shoulder/l_knee/r_knee (22-26)' to the creature rig that 'only MCSWolf allocates'. MCSCharacter.as:120 partListLength = 22 with the inclusive loop at :141 allocates index 22 on EVERY human; MCSCharacter.as:54 declares PART_prop3 = 22. So 22 cannot simultaneously be inside a 23-deep human stack and a creature-only extra. (It is true that no human code path READS partList[PART_prop3] - only MCSWolf.as:148 does - but 'allocates' is the wrong verb and it breaks the claim's own count.) Seven siblings in this packet state the boundary correctly, so nothing is lost by rejecting this one.

The cite is the refutation. It reads '(grep for the four constants returns only their declarations)' and the text asserts the four are 'declared but never used anywhere in the corpus'. My own grep -rn over reference/decompiled/ for PART_l_shoulder|PART_r_shoulder|PART_l_knee|PART_r_knee returns, besides the four declarations at MCSCharacter.as:56/58/60/62, four USES: MCSWolf.as:184 partList[PART_r_shoulder], :188 partList[PART_l_shoulder], :193 partList[PART_r_knee], :197 partList[PART_l_knee] - and the identical four in shs3_android_payload/. A cite asserting a grep result the grep does not produce is mis-cited under the cite lens, and the assertion is the exact opposite of what six of its own siblings establish. Its two asides do hold (StatsManager.as:3330 'case EQ_ACCESSORY1: getPlayerMCS().setProp2(itemid);' and setArmor reading 8 part containers) but they belong to a claim that is not this one.

Every count reproduces exactly from my own parse of all 412 <modifier> rows: 34 distinct ids; 47 rows in the 0-16 stat switch (11.4%); 344 rows in the 101-1999 Set band (83.5%); and 19 rows across 11 distinct ids (25x1, 38x6, 78x2, 79x2, 84x2, 90x1, 96x1, 97x1, 98x1, 99x1, 40000x1) falling outside both. XMLItem.as:288-296 is the default branch verbatim, and strings.json["123"] = 'Set' confirms the literal 'Set: <id>' rendering. Like its sibling it correctly excludes id 82 (Item.as:12 USESMODID). The lane point - that the dominant channel is set membership and needs a set-bonus table nobody has looked for - follows from the data.

Verified line for line. InventoryUI.refreshEquipment at :455-534 is a literal 'for(var i:int = 0; i < 9; i++)' switch: case 0 EQ_HAT->SLOT_HAT, 1 EQ_ARMOR, 2 EQ_GLOVES, 3 EQ_PANTS, 4 EQ_MASK, 5 EQ_WEAPON, 6 EQ_SHOES, 7 EQ_ACCESSORY1->SLOT_RING1, 8 EQ_ACCESSORY2->SLOT_RING2. EQ_NECK appears nowhere in the file. The sentinel ids are verbatim in the guard at :534: 'tempItem.getItemID() != 0 && != 4001 && != 4000 && != 11001'. Independently corroborated in the frame: my full-frame read of reference/frames/s21_weapon/t708.0.png shows exactly nine paperdoll boxes, two of them ring outlines, and no neck box. This is also the direct refutation of the build-provenance-drift claim in the same packet.

new_findings.text: All five XOR-obfuscated Android resource blobs decrypt and inflate, and 115_Mobile_SHS3Resource.bin IS the per-item art manifest. The cipher is in the corpus: ResourceManager.as:200-217 decryptByteArray touches only bytes 3..255 (with an i%11==0 swap to i+256) and the key is the SECOND CHARACTER OF THE RESOURCE FILENAME - Mobile.as:352 / ResourceManager.as:186 pass resourceFileNameArray[n].charCodeAt(1), and ResourceManager.as:41 names the five files. Keys are therefore h=104 (shs3resource), u=117 (musicresource), o=111 (soundresource), m=109 (imageresource), g=103 (bgresource). Running that over all five: 115 -> 1,040,849 B, 113 -> 1,402,677 B, 122 -> 29,623 B, 124 -> 1,908,229 B, 120 -> 4,412,340 B, every one a CWS v17 that zlib-inflates cleanly. Parsing SymbolClass/ExportAssets out of the inflated 115 yields 1,912 exported symbols whose prefixes are exactly the getMCSComponent partTypes: torso/stomach/uparm/lowarm/pelvic 151 each, item 112, weapon 109, hat 96, calf/crotch/thigh 85 each, skill 79, hair 73, prop 60, mask 59, foot/foottop 44 each, head 38, hand/neck 33 each, backleg/frontleg 12 each, tail 9, acc 8, achievement 5, plus *_wolf_ and *_horse_ creature sets. Sample names: item0, item1, item009, item010, item2100..., acc3000..acc3008, weapon13000..weapon13056. NOTE the C1 brief gives key 'm'=109 as the example; that is the IMAGE resource key specifically, not a single key for all five.

new_findings.lane_impact: L6 (art) - CLOSES the icon/art blocker outright rather than scoping it. The item####, acc####, weapon####, hat####, mask#### and paperdoll part symbol families the items-equipment survey calls unrecoverable are in a held file and enumerable today. It also invalidates any lane plan that budgets for authoring ~1,900 symbols from scratch, and it retires the last 'S0-5 stands' language wherever it survives.

new_findings.text: There is a THIRD border-colour tip that no claim in this packet cites, four lines above the blue one: GameEngine.as:564 'Tip: A green border indicates that an item is special.' Together with :568 (blue = rare) and :572 (purple = unique) the game's own tip list names three of the four getShopItemType() tiers, which is far stronger corroboration for the 4-tier border ladder than the two-tip argument the border claims actually make.
new_findings.quote: GameEngine.as:564 'str = "Tip: A green border indicates that an item is special.";' / :568 'str = "Tip: A blue border indicates that an item is rare.";' / :572 'str = "Tip: A purple border indicates that an item is unique.";'
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 (UI/HUD) + L6 (art) - the border tier names are green=special, blue=rare, purple=unique, with normal as the default tan. Any lane building the ShopItem border art now has a named colour for three of the four tiers straight from shipped in-game copy.

new_findings.text: The rarity colour key is exact and there are TWO palettes, not one. Item.as:417-434 (the branch taken when the loot dialog or gift dialog is up and the inventory is not) emits unique #b048f8, rare #0080ff, special #1eff00, normal #FFFFFF. The else branch starting Item.as:436 uses a darker set for the same ladder, beginning unique #6600cc. The same four-tier test - itemxml.unique == 1 OR isPickableQuestItem() OR itemID in 20103..20107 OR isPlayerNamed(), then mods>=3, then mods>0 - drives both, and is the same test as getShopItemType() at Item.as:382-404.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 (UI/HUD) - exact hex for the item-name colour ladder, and the fact that the loot/gift dialog uses a brighter palette than the inventory panel. A builder implementing one palette gets the loot popup wrong.

new_findings.text: MCSWolf's partList ends up 49 entries long, not 26. Its constructor calls super() FIRST (MCSWolf.as:11), which runs MCSCharacter's own loop and pushes 23 clips (indices 0..22); only then does it set partListLength = 25 (:13) and push 26 MORE (:14-18). Indices 23-26, which MCSWolf then binds as leg segments at :184/:188/:193/:197, therefore land in the second batch. Every claim in this packet that says 'MCSWolf raises partListLength to 25' is right about the field and silent about the list. A second consequence: MCSCharacter.as:246 'for(var i:* = int(this.partListLength - 1); i >= 0; i--)' walks only indices 24..0 on a wolf, so it never touches the upper half of that 49-entry list.
new_findings.quote: MCSWolf.as:11 'super();' / :13 'partListLength = 25;' / :14 'for(var i:int = 0; i <= partListLength; i++)' / :17 'partList.push(mc);'  ||  MCSCharacter.as:141 'for(var i:int = 0; i <= this.partListLength; i++)' with :120 'internal var partListLength:int = 22;'  ||  MCSCharacter.as:246 'for(var i:* = int(this.partListLength - 1); i >= 0; i--)'
new_findings.lane_impact: L6 (art/animation) - the creature-rig contract is not 'human 23 + 4 extras'. A wolf gets a fresh 26-slot block stacked on top of the inherited 23, and the PART_* indices 23-26 address the new block. Anyone porting the quadruped rig from the packet's partList claims will build the wrong container count and the wrong z-order for creatures.

new_findings.text: The web v0.717 half of the stance-gate claim was cited only as 'the documented Focus >= 48 gate' - a pointer to a document, not an artifact. It is in the payload: §1t99s0§.as:3058 opens the stance-rotation function (same four-way stance cycle as MCSPlayer.nextStance) and :3060 reads 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48) { return; }'. The canChangeStance mirror is :3043-3045 (identical actionState disjunction to MCSPlayer.as:2966) with :3050 'return this.§1t4469s0§() && this.§1t4414s0§ >= 48;'. Against §1t99s0§.as:249 '= 8 * 24' (192) that is a quarter bar, versus MCSPlayer.as:2977 'this.maxreload / 6' over MCSPlayer.as:239 '5 * 24' (120) = a sixth.
